title: Two pockets
hookLine: Rabbi Simcha Bunim: one note says "for my sake the world was made", the other "I am dust and ashes"
carry: know which pocket to reach into

cards: Some days you feel like nothing. A mistake at work, the wrong thing said, and the voice in your head says you don't matter at all.
Other days you feel like the center of the universe, and the voice says everyone should notice. Plenty of people swing between the two, sometimes in the same afternoon.
A Hasidic rebbe in Poland had a remedy that fits in your clothes. All you need is two pockets, and two slips of paper.

teach.b: Rabbi Simcha Bunim of Peshischa lived around 1800. He's remembered as a sharp, honest teacher who hated pretending. The teaching attributed to him goes like this: every person should have two pockets.
In one, a note that says: for my sake the world was created. In the other: I am dust and ashes. The wisdom is knowing which pocket to reach into, and when.
Both lines are old. You've met the first on this path: it's from the Mishnah, in tractate Sanhedrin.

teach.h: FOR MY SAKE THE WORLD WAS MADE.
teach.b: Because the first human being was created alone, each life is a whole world, so every person is obligated to say: for my sake the world was created. The second comes from Genesis.

teach.h: I AM BUT DUST AND ASHES.
teach.b: Abraham, bargaining with God to save the city of Sodom, stops himself and says he is "but dust and ashes." Here's the trick.

teach.h: REACH FOR THE ONE YOU NEED.
teach.b: When you're low, feeling worthless, reach into the first pocket: your life is a whole world. When you're puffed up, sure you're owed, reach into the second: you're dust and ashes, and so is everyone else.
Neither note alone is the truth. Carry only the first, and you grow arrogant. Carry only the second, and you're crushed.
Together they hold you in the middle, where Abraham stood: humble, and bold enough to argue with God.

how: Many Jews know Rabbi Simcha Bunim's two-pockets teaching, and some literally carry the two sayings on slips of paper as a reminder of balance between dignity and humility.

o: a rule to keep holy and everyday things apart
a reminder to give half of what you have away
two notes, one for dignity and one for humility

games.q: you made a mistake at work and feel like you're nothing. which pocket do you reach into?
o: for my sake the world was created.
games.why: when you're low, reach for the first note: each life is a whole world. the dust and ashes note is for when you're puffed up.

practice: Put one hand on your right side and think: for my sake the world was made; your life is a whole world. Put the other hand on your left and think, gently: I am dust and ashes.
Feel both at once, neither one crushing you or lifting you too high; some people even write the two lines on slips of paper and carry them.
